chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

A legal ruling was given regarding a female slave whom the son of her master sold while his father was absent. A man bought her, and she bore him a boy. Then the first master arrived and disputed with the final master, saying: 'This is my female slave; my son sold her without my permission.' He was told: 'Take your female slave and her son.' The buyer entreated him, saying: 'Take the son of the one who sold you the female slave,' meaning the son who sold her, 'until he completes for you what he sold you.' When the seller took the son, the father said to him: 'Send my son.' He replied: 'By Allah, I will not send your son until you send my son.' When the first master saw this, he ratified the sale of his son.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a son selling a female slave without his father's permission and the status of the child born to her?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the fiqh of 'ikrah' (compulsion) and conditional sales, where the father's refusal to release the son serves as leverage to validate the son's unauthorized sale of the slave. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the buyer retains the right to withhold the purchased item's offspring until the seller fulfills the condition of ratifying the transaction, ensuring equitable restitution. This case underscores the interplay between property rights and familial authority in classical Islamic commercial law.
